All nine files serve one concern, the task-management domain. There are three entities (Project, User, Task), a value type for task status (TaskStatus plus parseTaskStatus), one repository interface per entity, an IdGenerator port and one error hierarchy (DomainError and its subclasses).

The abstractions are used consistently:
- Every entity has a private constructor and a static create factory that validates input.
- Every entity reports invalid input with ValidationError from errors.ts.
- Task.markDone reports a conflict with ConflictError.
- The status rule lives only in task-status.ts. Task and TaskFilter use the TaskStatus type instead of redefining the allowed values.
- The repository interfaces follow the same save/findById shape.

The only near-duplicate is the trim-and-check-non-empty name logic in Project.create and User.create. Each check protects a different entity's own invariant, with its own error message, so it is not a single shared rule copied in two places. No file bypasses the module's abstractions.
